title: Reset a six-row 20-inch planter to four rows at 30 inches, centred on the hitch
instruction: Reset this planter from six rows at 20 inches to four rows at 30 inches. Move the green row units along the toolbar so that four of them stand upright on it, square to it and centred across its width, two on each side of the red centre mark, symmetric about the mark and 30 inches (190.5 mm at this 1:4 scale) apart centre to centre, with no unit on the mark. Stand the two spare units upright, one on each grey stand.
context: Farm equipment set-up. A row-crop planter's row units clamp along its toolbar, and the rows must match the combine head or sprayer that will work the field after it, so between seasons farm equipment mechanics and operators (O*NET 49-3041, 45-2091) re-space the units: they unclamp them, move them along the bar and set each one with a tape from the toolbar's centre (the hitch), so the rows sit symmetric about the tractor; units not needed come off onto stands. Six rows at 20 in and four at 30 in both span 120 in, so one toolbar carries either. With an even number of rows no unit sits on the centre line: the two middle rows are half a spacing either side of it. At this 1:4 scale the four rows go 95.25 and 285.75 mm either side of the centre mark; the six start at 63.5, 190.5 and 317.5 mm. Neither new position is marked: they follow from the spacing, the row count and the mark. Each arm naturally resets its own side.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A row-crop planter at 1:4 scale; four kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Toolbar: a dark-grey steel bar fixed to the table, 700 mm long along y, 40 mm wide along x and 30 mm tall, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0 (x 28.0 to 32.0 cm, y -35.0 to +35.0 cm); its flat top is 30 mm above the table. A red centre mark 10 mm wide is painted across its top and faces at y 0 (y -0.5 to +0.5 cm); in simulation the bar is three boxes with one flush top, two grey halves and the red mark between them. (2) Hitch tongue: a dark-grey steel box fixed to the table on the midline, 100 mm along x, 30 mm wide and 25 mm tall (x 18.0 to 28.0 cm, y -1.5 to +1.5 cm), butting the toolbar's face nearest the arms; it shows where the tractor is and nothing goes on it. (3) Two spare-unit stands: light-grey rigid plastic plates fixed to the table, 90 x 90 mm and 10 mm thick, sides parallel to x and y, centred at x 17.0 cm, y +25.0 cm (left) and y -25.0 cm (right). (4) Six row units: loose green-painted wooden blocks standing in for planter row units, all alike, 70 mm long (along x), 36 mm wide (along y) and 45 mm tall, 80 g each, their top and bottom alike. They stand upright on the toolbar's top, long side along x (square to the bar), centred on its centre line (x 30.0 cm) and overhanging it 15 mm front and back like a clamp bracket, as six rows 20 in (127 mm at 1:4) apart, symmetric about the mark: centres at y +6.35, +19.05 and +31.75 cm (left) and -6.35, -19.05 and -31.75 cm (right), 91 mm of clear bar between neighbours. Nothing else is on the table. The four rows at 30 in (190.5 mm) that the instruction asks for have their centres 95.25 mm and 285.75 mm either side of the mark: on each side the inner unit moves out 31.75 mm, the outer one moves in 31.75 mm and the middle one comes off onto that side's stand (any unit may take any place).
scoring: End state: the score is read from where the six units are at the last step, measured along the toolbar from the centre of the red mark (y 0). A unit's tilt is the angle of its 45 mm height from vertical, either way up. A unit is 'on the toolbar' when its centre, seen from above, is over the toolbar's top and its lowest point is within 3 mm of that top (set square, turned or tipped over). It is 'set' when it is on the toolbar, tilted at most 5 degrees, its long side within 8 degrees of x (square to the bar) and its centre within 12 mm of the bar's centre line (x 28.8 to 31.2 cm). It 'stands on' a stand when its centre is over that stand's 90 x 90 mm top, its lowest point within 3 mm of that top and it is tilted at most 5 degrees. A unit belongs to the side of the mark its centre is on (left y > 0, right y < 0). Score 0 if any unit is off the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top) or any unit on the toolbar has its centre within 23 mm of the mark's centre, so that it covers part of the mark (a row on the centre line, the odd-row layout). Otherwise each side scores on its own and the score is their sum. A side scores 0.5 if exactly two units are on that side of the toolbar, both set, one with its centre 85.25 to 105.25 mm from the mark (95.25 within 10 mm) and the other 275.75 to 295.75 mm from it (285.75 within 10 mm), and a unit stands on that side's stand. It scores 0.25 if exactly two units are on that side of the toolbar, both set, within 25 mm of those two distances, and one of the two 0.5 conditions holds: both within 10 mm (its stand empty) or a unit standing on its stand (a row 10 to 25 mm off). Otherwise 0: three units still on it, one or none, a unit turned or tipped on the bar, one more than 25 mm off (the old 20 in positions are 31.75 mm off), or a row 10 to 25 mm off with the stand empty. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Every outcome: the start (three units each side): 0; only the spares taken off, the four left at 63.5 and 317.5 mm: 0; four kept at the old 63.5 and 190.5 mm: 0; three rows at 30 in (0 and +-190.5 mm): 0; one side done, the other as found: 0.5; one side at 0.25 (rows done, spare not on its stand; or spare on its stand, a row 10 to 25 mm off), the other as found: 0.25; one side done, the other at 0.25: 0.75; both at 0.25: 0.5; both done: 1.0. Any unit may take any place. A spare not on a stand may be anywhere off the toolbar (on the table, held, on another unit). The trial ends early once 1.0 has held with every unit still (its centre moving less than 5 mm in all over the last 0.5 s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, tape each unit's centre (half-way between its side faces) from the centre of the red mark along the bar, check it square with a try square against the bar's face, and check each spare stands on its stand.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction; the toolbar, hitch and stands are fixed boxes. Real row units weigh tens of kilograms, hang on a parallel linkage, clamp on with U-bolts and are slid along the bar on a jack; here each is an 80 g block at 1:4, lifted and set down, and nothing clamps. The 10 mm tolerance (1.6 in at full size) is looser than a real set-up's (about 0.5 in): the arms trail their commands by a few mm. The scorer sees only the units, so one held still in place counts as set.
reset_notes: Stand the six units back upright and square on the toolbar's top, long side along x, centred on its centre line (x 30.0 cm), at y +6.35, +19.05, +31.75, -6.35, -19.05 and -31.75 cm (six rows at 20 in, 1:4). The toolbar, hitch tongue and stands are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
